purpose: Framework-level validation: does the self-improvement loop produce, gate and (if admitted) deploy a real change on a wider development split?
known_boundaries: Every case is inside datasets/protocols/development_exposure.json, so no reading is a generalization claim.
The split is disjoint (pool vs validation) but was not audited by an independent party.
The mock dry run of the same config produced zero families; that says nothing about the real detector.
One earlier single-case probe did not finish in 20 minutes, so per-case latency has a long tail and the wall-clock estimate is uncertain.
The cycle wall-clock cap and worker count were raised after measuring latency; the measurement design (split, gates, thresholds) was not changed.

engineering: three cycles complete or stop for a recorded reason
no gate is relaxed and no threshold is edited
effect: at least one candidate reaches a gate verdict on a real batch
if a candidate is admitted, the version record is written and the next cycle loads it
if nothing is admitted, the readings still distinguish 'instrument could not measure' from 'mechanism failed'

not_success: any admission obtained by widening a gate, swapping a batch after seeing output, or dropping failures from the report
reporting a single-case repair as evidence of a mechanism

attempts.reason_for_restart: attempt 2 froze after cycle 1 on a defect in the framework itself, not in the candidate: the defect-injection audit swept the whole batch for unmeasurable rows and treated the presence of one as disqualifying. A single sentinel case (Octotools/008) hit its 3600s case deadline, so the audit went inconclusive and the frozen verdict ended the three-cycle run.
attempts.fix: evolution/engine.py: the audit now re-derives the defect rejection with the unmeasurable rows excluded, instead of refusing to certify whenever any background case degrades. Insufficient-coverage detection is kept as a separate condition. 6 new tests in test_audit_inconclusive_scope.py; full suite 503 passed.
attempts.scope_unchanged: 3 cycles / pool 44 / patrol 20 / sentinel 6+6 / gain 8 / all gates untouched
attempts.cache_invalidated: source_digest() covers evolution/*.py and detector/*.py, so the engine fix changed the cache namespace and the checkpoint contract source digest (d23c003d6a90791b -> 014fdb6135ef7318). Attempt 3 therefore re-measures the sentinel and gain cases instead of replaying attempt 2's cache. This is the designed fail-safe -- a cached result produced by different gate logic must not be reused -- and it is the honest reason attempt 3 is slower than a pure re-launch.
attempts.known_cost: The audit re-runs whenever the active registry or the source changes, so each cycle that admits a candidate pays roughly one extra S+G wave for the audit.
attempts.outcome: operator stopped it after 18 of 40 cycle-1 rows because the audit fix had exposed the next blocker: the per-case measurement envelope was itself cutting cases. One of 18 rows (Octotools/008) was cut at exactly the 3600s case deadline -- its terminal basis is 'case_deadline_exceeded', with 6 defense attempts and one judge vote lost to a transport timeout -- so it returned degraded_judge_only and could not be scored. A second row (Camel/048) completed authoritatively at 3600.139s, i.e. 139ms past the same deadline, because the deadline is only checked before each call. A cut call returns nothing and burns its whole budget, and because the two arms run at different times a cut can land on one arm alone, which HARMLESSNESS (new_unresolved_allowed=0) then reads as a regression the candidate caused.
attempts.correction: An earlier archive note listed both Octotools/008 and Camel/048 as cut. That was wrong: it was inferred from elapsed >= 3599, and Camel/048's own result is authoritative with every stage 'ok'. The archive's archive.json has been corrected to record only Octotools/008 as cut, with Camel/048 recorded as a near-miss.

attempts.reason_for_restart: the case-timeout investigation the operator asked for found the cause and it was not the case deadline. Reasoning length is stochastic: one identical prompt produced 36 and 13,437 reasoning tokens on different calls (median 2,113) at 20-46 tok/s, so a legitimate deliberation routinely needs more than the 300s per-attempt cap. Every call that did was killed mid-flight and retried from scratch, paying the first attempt's tokens and wall clock twice over.

measurement.probe: output/selfevo-run/timeout_probe.py -- same prompt, zero concurrency, 2 calls: 802 completion tokens / 23.4s then 11,365 / 546.5s (attempts=2). The second call exceeded 300s on its first attempt and was retried.
measurement.envelope_probe: output/selfevo-run/timeout_envelope_probe.py -- under the old cap no single attempt can exceed 300s by construction; under the new envelope single attempts ran 42s (2,746 tokens) and 187.8s.
measurement.thinking_probe: output/selfevo-run/thinking_probe.py -- 5 thinking controls on one prompt. All were accepted, and disabling thinking cuts a call to 43-90 tokens in 2-14s. It also changes the verdict on a known error case: the reasoning baseline says error, while thinking-disabled, enable_thinking_false and reasoning_effort_none all say clean. So the fast path is not a free speedup -- it would replace the deliberation the detector exists to perform. Not adopted.
measurement.retry_amplification: Across the run's cache, judge needed 44 extra attempts over 25 cases, defense 17 over 9, and the causal upgrade 20 over 7, beyond their configured ballots.
measurement.token_undercount: A voting stage reports its LAST ballot's provider meta, so 'usage' records one ballot of three. Judge and defense carried 3 ballots plus up to 2 topups. The reported 120,331 completion tokens for 18 rows is therefore a floor, not the burn. Fixed: detector/provider.py accumulate_usage() folds every ballot into a new 'usage_total' beside the old field, which is left intact for existing readers.

evolution/configs/validation_big_run.jso.why: a case may now take up to 3h, and a cycle is about ten serial case evaluations; a 5h cycle cap would fail-close the tail of every cycle to unresolved, which reads as unmeasured rather than as a mechanism failure

envelope_change.why_this_is_not_relaxing_a_gate: These are runtime envelopes and token ceilings, not admission thresholds. No gate, no split, no case set and no metric definition changed. tests/test_repository.py pins the new floors so the envelope cannot silently regress, with the measurement written into the comment.

attempts.conclusion: The localization objective is a capability limitation of the action space on this corpus, not a framework defect: classify_family_actionability offers a FAM-loc- family exactly one route (tracer_directive), the tracer's own TRACER_SYSTEM already commands the procedure a directive would paraphrase, and a directive that contradicts it is overruled by the stage's contract. The framework correctly refused to admit five inert candidates.

concurrency_measurement.explanation: The engine evaluates in waves (sentinel -> gain -> patrol), and each wave's concurrency is bounded by that wave's case count, not by the configured worker setting. During the tail of the 12-case sentinel wave only 2 cases remain, so exactly 2 provider calls are in flight. Observed worker PIDs rotate as calls finish, so this is a wave tail and not a stall.
concurrency_measurement.why_not_raise_concurrency: Wave sizes are 12 (sentinel), 8 (gain) and 20 (patrol over 44 pool cases). Concurrency above 20 cannot speed up the first two waves at all and only helps the patrol wave from 20 to 24.
concurrency_measurement.per_case_call_count: One case is several sequential provider calls: judge takes 3 votes, then recall/upgrade/tracer, then defense takes 3 votes plus top-ups. That is why a case can occupy 10-25 minutes even though each call is one worker.
